stem.en: A grower uses cuttings for a plantation and seeds for a breeding programme. Which pair of reasons is correct?

text.en: Cuttings give fast copies; seeds give new mixes.

feedback.en: Correct. Copies keep one good variety, and seeds bring variation.

text.en: Cuttings give new mixes; seeds give exact copies of the parent.

feedback.en: It is the other way round. Cuttings are copies of one plant.

text.en: Cuttings need two parents; seeds need only a single parent.

feedback.en: It is the other way round. A cutting comes from one parent.

text.en: Both give identical plants, but seeds simply take far longer.

feedback.en: Plants from seeds differ from each other, as they come from two gametes.

explanation.en: A cutting comes from one parent, so it is a fast copy of a good variety. Seeds come from fertilisation, so they carry a new mix of characters, which is what a breeder looks for.

hints.en: How many parents does each method use?
